data.title: Contrast
data.tagline: Contrast is the brightness difference between text and background—big enough to read; light gray on light gray is not.
data.learningOutcome: You can turn "hard to read" into a contrast requirement (4.5:1 for body) and know to re-check dark mode.
data.description: Light gray body text on a gray background almost vanishes when you squint—that is insufficient contrast. To turn "hard to read" into a checkable requirement, tell the AI "keep body text at 4.5:1 contrast against the background," the common industry threshold. Dark mode fails here most often: black backgrounds paired with the old gray look layered but sit below the line.

learning.assumes: You have struggled to read a phone screen in sunlight.
learning.outcome: You can turn "hard to read" into a contrast requirement (4.5:1 for body) and know to re-check dark mode.

distinctions.label: Dark mode
distinctions.explanation: Dark Mode flips the palette; Contrast is what you re-check afterwards so text stays readable on the new background.

distinctions.label: Typography
distinctions.explanation: Typography sizes and weights text for scanning; Contrast decides whether that text is readable against its background at all.

explanation.title: Readable text 4.5:1
explanation.text: Headings, body, captions, button labels—everything meant for real reading needs at least 4.5:1 against its background.

explanation.title: Large text and icons 3:1
explanation.text: Big headlines, icons, and button borders that carry no paragraph-level reading duty start at 3:1—anything lower becomes invisible.

data.boundary: Contrast is not "do the colors look good"—aesthetics is a separate question; contrast only answers legibility. It covers more than text: icons, button borders, and form outlines have thresholds too. Re-check dark mode separately instead of reusing the light-mode text colors.

lessonPractice.title: After dark mode ships, someone says the body text strains their eyes. Which description most likely pinpoints the problem?

options.label: Check whether body text contrast reaches 4.5:1
options.feedback: Correct. The background turned black while the text kept its gray, dropping below the threshold. The ratio gives the AI a concrete target.

options.label: Bump the body font two sizes larger so words are easier to make out
options.feedback: Larger type stays hard to read if the color difference is unchanged; check contrast first.

options.label: Switch the text to a brighter brand color so it stands out more
options.feedback: A different color is not automatically compliant—bright may pass on black and fail on gray; verify by ratio.

data.agentPrompt: Fix the low-contrast text on the page: readable text versus background at least 4.5:1, large headlines and icons at least 3:1, and re-check in dark mode. List which colors you changed.
